prerequisites: basic knowledge of calculus (differential and integral calculus, ordinary differential equations)
minimal familiarity with the Matlab computing environment

learning_outcomes.text: describe the concept of dynamical system and its mathematical representations (input–state–output and, for LTI systems, transfer function)
understand the balance equations and constitutive laws underlying lumped-parameter physical modelling across different domains (mechanical, thermal, fluidic, electrical/electronic)
recognise the analogies between physical domains and multi-domain interactions
understand the fundamentals of numerical methods for the integration of differential equations and the concepts of stability, accuracy and stiffness
procedures for deriving lumped-parameter models starting from a real physical system
parameter identification techniques on experimental data (least squares) and model validation
numerical simulation methods in the Matlab/Simulink environment, with an appropriate choice of solvers and integration steps
parametric analyses and comparison between simulated results and experimental data
the adequacy of a model with respect to its purpose, managing the trade-off between accuracy and complexity
the quality of an identified model through the analysis of errors, residuals and overfitting phenomena
the reliability of simulation results in relation to numerical stability and error
the modelling choices and their results through clear and reproducible technical reports
the interpretation of simulation results with appropriate use of terminology, units of measurement and graphical representations
autonomously extend the acquired methodologies to new systems and application domains
consult technical and scientific documentation (including the official MathWorks documentation) to deepen tools and methods
independently tackle modelling and simulation problems in professional contexts or in subsequent studies

syllabus_topics: Introduction to system modelling (fundamentals) Concept of a model: purpose, level of detail, accuracy/complexity trade-off. System, subsystem, boundaries, state variables, inputs, outputs, disturbances. System classification: SISO/MIMO, LTI/nonlinear, continuous-time/discrete-time, deterministic/stochastic (overview)

Physical lumped-parameter modelling and multi-domain analogies Balances and constitutive laws: conservation principles and dynamics. Typical structures: storage, dissipation, conversion elements. Mathematical analogies across domains (e.g., electrical–mechanical–thermal–fluidic). Cross-domain examples (depending on the degree programme): RLC networks and circuit models (electronics). Mass–spring–damper models (mechanics). RC thermal models (thermal systems). Tank and pipe models (fluid systems)

Mathematical representations of dynamic systems Ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and nonlinear models. Input–state–output form: definition and physical interpretation of states. Relationship with the transfer function for LTI systems. Subsystem interconnections: series/parallel/feedback, modular modelling

Identification and validation (operational introduction) Why identification is needed: uncertain parameters and data-informed models. Parameter fitting from experimental data: least squares (basics), model selection, model/data comparison. Quality metrics and validation (error, residuals, overfitting: essential concepts)

Numerical simulation ODE integration methods: Euler, Runge–Kutta (concepts), adaptive solvers. Numerical stability, local/global error, step-size choice. Stiff systems: recognition and impact on simulation (overview). Discretisation and discrete-time simulation: sampling, aliasing (essential reminders)

Modelling and simulation in Matlab/Simulink (guided lab) Model implementation in Matlab: scripts, functions, simulation and post-processing. Simulink: block-based modelling, solver settings, parameters, signal logging. Parametric analyses, scenarios, parameter sweeps, comparison of modelling architectures. Good practices: traceability, units, lightweight model versioning, simulation reporting
Case studies focused on electronics and biomedicine
teaching_methods: Guided laboratory activities in the Matlab/Simulink environment

assessment_methods.method: Discussion of a report/activity carried out in the Matlab/Simulink environment

assessment_rules: Learning is assessed through a final examination. The examination includes applied exercises and theory questions, and is complemented by the discussion of a report/activity carried out in the Matlab/Simulink environment. The assessment, expressed out of thirty, considers correctness and completeness in solving exercises, command of theoretical fundamentals, appropriateness of technical language, ability to justify modelling choices, and critical interpretation of simulation results. The examination is passed with a minimum mark of 18/30; honours are awarded for full command, autonomy of judgement, and particular clarity of exposition.
